modified_caption: The line plot depicts the performance of various model editing techniques on Llama2, measured by accuracy percentage (ACC) across an increasing number of co-occurrences. The x-axis, labeled 'Co-occurrence Number,' spans an exponential scale from 1 to over 1000, while the y-axis, labeled 'ACC (%),' ranges linearly from 60% to 80%. Six techniques are compared: Base (black, circular markers), FT (blue, downward triangles), IKE (red, upward triangles), MEND (brown, diamonds), MEMIT (purple, pentagons), and ROME (green, squares). The ROME method consistently outperforms all others, achieving an accuracy of approximately 77% at the highest co-occurrence value. The MEND and MEMIT techniques exhibit nearly identical performance, stabilizing around 70% accuracy beyond 100 co-occurrences. Notably, the FT method demonstrates a marked decline in accuracy after 100 co-occurrences, dropping to roughly 62% at the highest value. The Base method shows the least improvement, plateauing at around 66%. The IKE method, while initially competitive, is eventually surpassed by both MEND and MEMIT, finishing at just under 68%. Overall, the data reveal that advanced editing techniques like ROME and MEND yield superior and more stable performance across varying co-occurrence levels.

modifications.claim: The FT method demonstrates a marked decline in accuracy after 100 co-occurrences, dropping to roughly 62% at the highest value.
modifications.reality: The FT method (blue line) shows a gradual increase in accuracy, reaching slightly above 68% at the highest co-occurrence value, with no decline.

modifications.claim: The MEND and MEMIT techniques exhibit nearly identical performance, stabilizing around 70% accuracy beyond 100 co-occurrences.
modifications.reality: MEND (brown) stabilizes around 73%, while MEMIT (purple) stabilizes around 72%, not 70%. They are close but not nearly identical, and the values are misrepresented.

modifications.claim: The IKE method, while initially competitive, is eventually surpassed by both MEND and MEMIT, finishing at just under 68%.
modifications.reality: The IKE method (red) finishes at just under 69%, not 68%, and is surpassed only by MEND, not MEMIT, which remains below MEND throughout.
